text:
maria: FYI we're getting a cluster of SSO refresh failures since the RBAC backfill started an hour ago. Customers reporting app loop on login.

sam: noticed spikes in token exchange errors. refresh endpoint returning invalid_grant for some service accounts. quick log snippet: 

auth-service stderr:
```
2026-03-21T22:11:03Z ERROR token_exchange.go:124 refresh failed sub=svc-824 invalid_grant: refresh token is invalid or revoked
```

dave: SCIM worker retried a bunch of creates right around that time — Okta returned intermittent 500s. Our create path currently inserts then dedupes, so we ended up with duplicate service_account rows with same external_id.

jessica: that matches: token issuance maps by external_id -> internal id. If there are two records with same ext_id, an issued token tied to the older internal id will fail to validate against the new one. Could show up as invalid_grant.

maria: also seeing KMS decrypt errors around 22:10 UTC. @kms-rot8-bot posted: 
```
ALERT decrypt: InvalidCiphertextException Key=projects/redwood/keys/ssoproxy-key version=3
```

sam: if key v2->v3 rotation happened during a short overlap, some clusters could be signing with v2 while others try to decrypt with v3. Combine that with duplicate records and we get intermittent invalid_grant. Need to check rotation timing and IAM changes.

alice: pulling audit now. No revoke calls from auth-service linked to the backfill job. I do see role binding changes and service principal permission tweaks but no explicit token revocations.

dave: confirmed SCIM retry behavior caused duplicates. Backfill changed role bindings on two service principals which kicked off a permission refresh flow. My hunch: token signed before rotate + lookup ambiguity = failed exchange.

jessica: immediate mitigations we should do now: 
- pause SCIM retry worker to stop more duplicates
- apply DB-level unique constraint on external_id (fast migration) and start dedupe/merge job
- pause KMS auto-rotation until we validate rolling handlers
- temporary auth fallback: if ext_id resolves to multiple internal ids, try each candidate when validating refresh tokens instead of rejecting immediately

sam: on KMS and logs. Exporting audit: s3://redwood-audit/exp/ssoprobs/1791234567.csv and requesting infra snapshot of key versions.

infra: snapshot shows ssoproxy-key rotations: v1->v2 at 2026-03-21T21:58Z, v2->v3 at 2026-03-21T22:09Z. There is an ~11s overlap where some clusters accepted v3 and others still had v2 cached.

maria: overlap + duplicate ext_ids seems like a plausible root cause. We should notify impacted customers and offer a forced refresh (invalidate refresh tokens from window) as a remediation.

alice: audit export lists 23 affected tenants (redacted). I'll attach to the incident ticket.

sam: quick triage: no signs of malicious key access, IAM looks unchanged. This is operational (rotation timing + SCIM idempotency). Opening a vuln/Ops ticket to track rotation tooling atomicity improvements.

dave: started DB migration: add unique index on service_accounts(external_id) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, plus a cleanup job that will merge duplicate rows and reassign tokens. PR: https://git.redwood.internal/p/scim/merge-extid-atomic

maria: need a rollback plan for the RBAC backfill in case mitigation fails. Reverting naive backfill might re-trigger SCIM events.

jessica: rollback runbook proposal: 1) disable SCIM worker 2) revert backfill changes 3) run merge/cleanup job 4) re-enable SCIM worker. I'll own verification and audit after each step.

sec-oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-0421-SSO-RB-02 created and assigned to @maria @sam @dave. Priority P1 :rotating_light:

sam: ETA ~45m for full root-cause writeup and recommended customer mitigation (scheduled short maintenance + forced refresh). Will update in 30.

dave: PR submitted, includes short-circuit dedupe path and idempotent create for SCIM to avoid future races.

maria: action items recap:
- sam: confirm KMS pause + produce rotation timeline (in progress)
- dave: DB migration + merge cleanup job (PR up)
- jessica: rollback runbook + audit verification
- alice: customer list + comms draft for status page

jessica: postmortem owners: security + infra + scim. We'll add a regression test covering rotation overlap and SCIM idempotency.

maria: copy. Escalating to product for status page and legal for compliance check.

alice: quick runbook note for responders: if you see invalid_grant + duplicate ext_id -> check (1) duplicate service_account rows, (2) KMS key version overlap, (3) audit for revoke calls, in that order.

sam: update 30m: KMS auto-rotate paused; no IAM policy changes detected; prepping customer-safe script to invalidate refresh tokens issued during rotation window (requires approval).

maria: approved. Keep this thread as canonical coordination channel. :lock:
